title: Blue Devils get stranded in Dallas and recruit Smith
summary: The Blue Devils, his first big band, got stranded in Dallas and drummer Ernest Williams came to Smith's house to hire him; he played clarinet and alto though he could not read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: No. Never did. When I joined up the big band... The biggest band I joined in them days, the first big band in fact, was the Blue Devils. And they came...
That was in about 1925?
Yeah.
And you were playing only alto with them. Or did you play clarinet?
Yes, I played clarinet and alto. I told them 'I can't read.' 'That's all right. Read the (?) books, and you can start right on the course.'
How did they get to hear about you? Did they hear you play
Buster Smith - 10
someplace?
Yeah.
Or did you go and sit in with them?

No. They came here in the summer, and hung out here. In fact, they got here and got stranded around here. Yeah. They came here with about eight pieces and they got stranded around here, and couldn't get out of town. So they stayed around here about a year-and-a-half or two years, and they geared the band back up. And Ernest Williams came out to my house and got me.
He was just the vocalist, or...?
No, he played drums.
He was the drummer with the band?
Yeah, he was the drummer with the band.
Because at one stage, you had this man, Willie McWashington, didn't you? You had him on drums at some stage, didn't you?
No.
With the Blue Devils?
No. We had this boy right here.
Oh, maybe Willie McWashington was with Bennie Moten.
Yeah. He was with Bennie Moten. Ernest Williams.
[EDWARD McNEIL IS CITED AS THE BLUE DEVILS' DRUMMER IN JAZZ STYLE IN K.C. & THE SOUTHWEST]
That's the drummer we had.
He is not living now.
Buster Smith - 11
Yeah! He's in Kansas City. If you go down there at the Palm Beach Club, you'll find he's down there every day. On (?) and Oakland(?). He's there every day.
